As for the one who said ḍāza yaḍūzu, its noun is ḍawzā, like shawrā.

Inna hiya, meaning these idols, illā asmā'un sammaytumūhā antum wa-ābā'ukum mā anzala Allāhu bihā min sulṭān (They are only names which you and your fathers have named; Allah has sent down no authority for them). The common reading is with yā' (in yattabiʿūna); ʿIsa read it with tā'. Illā al-ẓanna (except conjecture) in their saying that they are gods and that they are their intercessors, wa-mā tahwā al-anfusu (and what the souls desire). And He has certainly sent them guidance from their Lord, to show that they are not gods, and that worship is fit only for Allah, the One, the Subduer.

And He certainly saw him another time, a second descent (nazlah ukhra), and He called it a "descent" by way of metaphor. This is because Jibril (Gabriel) was seen by the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) in the form in which he was created, twice: once at the highest horizon on earth, and once near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha) in the heavens. This is the view of ʿĀ'ishah and most of the scholars, and it is the preferred one, because He linked the seeing with a place when He said ʿinda sidrat al-muntahā, and because He said nazlatan ukhrā, whose implied meaning is: "He saw him descending another time." Attributing place and descent, which is movement, to God is impossible. Also, He said nazlatan ukhrā, and it is not reported in any hadith that the Prophet ﷺ saw his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, before the night of the Ascension (mi'raj) and then saw Him again that night. What supports this is:

ʿaqil ibn Muhammad informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: ʿAbd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, who said: Dawud ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, from Masruq, that ʿĀ'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has greatly slandered Allah."

He said: I was reclining, so I sat up and said: "O Mother of the Believers, grant me a moment and do not hurry. Tell me about the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And he certainly saw him another time﴾ and ﴿And he certainly saw him at the clear horizon﴾." She said: "It was only Jibril. He saw him in his form in which he was created, twice: once when he descended from the sky to the earth, filling the greatest span between the sky and the earth, and once near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary." She said: "And I was the first to ask the Prophet about this verse, and he said: 'It is Jibril.'" [124]

ʿinda sidrat al-muntahā: ʿinda is connected to his saying ra'āhu (he saw him). The sidrah is the lote-tree (shajrat al-nabiq). It was called "the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary" because the knowledge of every knower ends at it.

Hilal ibn Sayyaf said: Ibn ʿAbbas asked Kaʿb about the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary while I was present, and Kaʿb said: "It is a lote-tree at the base of the Throne, on the heads of the bearers of the Throne, and the knowledge of creation ends at it, and what lies beyond it is unseen, which none knows except Allah, the Glorified."

Ibn Masʿud said: it was named so because what descends from above it and what ascends from below it, of the command of Allah, the Exalted, ends at it. When one who ascends to it from the earth reaches it, it is seized from it. It was also said: it is because the spirits of believers ascend and end at it. And it was said: it is because everyone who dies upon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah and his way ends at it.

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu al-ʿĀliyah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey (usriya bihi), he reached the Lote-tree, and it was said to him: "This is the Lote-tree, to which every one of your community who follows your Sunnah will come." Behold, from its root flow rivers of water unaltered (ghayru asin) up to His saying: "purified" (muṣaffā). It is a tree under whose shade a rider travels for seventy years without crossing it, and one of its leaves covers the whole community.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shaybah narrated to us, who said: al-Tanukhi narrated to us, who said: ʿUbayd ibn Yaʿish narrated to us, who said: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, from Yahya ibn ʿAbbad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from his grandmother Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ mention the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, and he said:

"A rider travels in the shade of its branch for a hundred years, and a hundred riders can take shelter in its branches. In it are golden butterflies, and its fruits are like jars (qilal)." [125] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/86, with slight variation]]

Muqatil said: It is a tree such that if one of its leaves were placed on the earth, it would light up for the people of the earth; it bears ornaments, garments and fruits of every colour. And if a man were to ride a swift she-camel and go around its trunk, he would not reach the place from which he set out until old age killed him. It is the Tuba (ṭūbā) which Allah mentioned in Surat al-Raʿd. I have fully described its attributes in the account of the Night Journey.

ʿindahā jannat al-maʾwā, idh yaghshā al-sidrata mā yaghshā (Near it is the Garden of Refuge, when there covers the Lote-tree what covers).

Ibn Masʿud and his companions said: "Golden butterflies." This is also the narration of al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas, and he traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ.

Al-Hasan said: The light of the Lord of Majesty covered it and it became radiant. It was also said: the angels.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw on every leaf of it an angel standing, glorifying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [126]

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu Hurayrah or another, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote-tree. He said: The light of creation covered it, and the angels covered it out of love for Allah, like crows when they alight on a tree.

He said: Then He spoke to him at that moment and said: "Ask."

In a hadith: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Then there covered it [in the source: yaghshāhā] a fluttering of green birds." [127] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/97.]]

Al-Suddi said: "Of birds, above it."

Anas narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I reached the Lote-tree, and I knew that it was the Lote-tree; I know its leaves and its fruit, and when its ripe fruit is like jars, and its leaves like elephants' ears. When there covered it of the command of Allah what covered it, it turned into rubies and emeralds, until no one can describe it. Near it is the Garden of Refuge." [128] [[See Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/72071; the hadith is not one single report.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is the right side of the Throne, and it is the station of the martyrs, like His saying: ﴿For them are the Gardens of Refuge﴾.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbd Allah ʿUmar ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Harith al-Qadibani narrated to us. He said: ʿAli ibn al-ʿAbbas al-Muqanaʿi narrated to us, who said: Maymun ibn al-Asbaʿ narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Salih al-Wuhadhi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Hamzah al-Basri narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr recite this verse as ʿindahā jannah (with a hā' at the end), meaning "the garden of spending the night" (jannat al-mabit).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and ʿUbayd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid narrated to us, who said: Abu Sadaqah narrated to me, who said: Abu al-Asbat narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, from ʿAli ibn al-Qasim al-Kindi, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi recite jannah al-maʾwā (with a hā'). Mujahid said: he means ajannahu (He covered him), and the hā' in this reading refers to the Prophet ﷺ.

Abu Hatim said: This is the reading of ʿAli and Anas, meaning "covered him." Al-Akhfash said: "reached him" (adrakahu).

Mā zāgha al-baṣaru wa-mā ṭagha (His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress): that is, he did not go beyond what he was commanded, nor did he turn away from what he was sent to see.

Laqad raʾā min āyāti rabbihi al-kubrā (He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord): that is, the greatest sign.

Ibn Masʿud said: He saw a green fluttering from Paradise that filled the horizon. Al-Dahhak said: the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He saw Jibril in his form which he has in the heavens. It was also said: the Ascension (al-miʿraj), and what was shown to him that night in his journey and his return and his beginning. The proof is His saying: ﴿So that We may show you of Our greatest signs﴾ ...

Afa-ra'aytumu al-lāt (Have you considered al-Lat?). The common reading is with the tā' lightened. It is derived from (Allah), and a tā' was added to it, so it became feminine. Just as it is said ʿumar for the male, then ʿumrah for the female, and ʿabbās and ʿabbāsah. Likewise the polytheists named their idols after the names of Allah: they said from Allah (al-Lāt), and from al-ʿAzīz (al-ʿUzzā).

Qatadah said: As for al-Lat, it was at al-Ta'if. Ibn Zayd said: al-Lat was a house at Nakhlah which Quraysh worshipped.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid and Abu Salih read al-Lāt with the tā' doubled, and they said: he was a man who used to pound (yaltu) sawiq for the pilgrims. When he died, they devoted themselves to his grave and worshipped him. Al-Suddi narrated from Abu Salih that he was at al-Ta'if, and he used to attend to their gods and pound sawiq for them; when he died, they worshipped him.

Mujahid said: He was a man on the top of a mountain who had goats from which he would collect butter and take aqit (dried curd), and gather their milk, and then prepare from it hays (a mixture of dates, aqit and ghee) which he fed to the pilgrims. He was at Batn Nakhlah, and when he died they worshipped him, and he is al-Lat. Al-Kalbi said: He was a man from Thaqif called Sakhrah ibn Ghanm, who used to melt butter and place it on a rock, and the Arabs would come and smear their swords with it. When the man died, Thaqif took the rock to their dwellings and worshipped it; the idol of al-Ta'if was based on the placing of al-Lat.

Wal-ʿUzzā: they differed about it. Mujahid said: It is a tree belonging to Ghatafan, which they worshipped.

It was this that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Khalid ibn al-Walid against, and he cut it down, and Khalid began striking it with an axe, saying:

"O ʿUzza, disbelief in you! No glory to you! Indeed I have seen that Allah has humiliated you."

From it there came out a female devil, with hair flowing and crying out woe, placing her hand on her head. It is said that Khalid returned to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "I have cut it down." He said: "What did you see?" He said: "I saw nothing." He said: "You have not cut it." So he went back to it with the axe, uprooted it and pulled out its root, and out came a naked woman, and he killed her. Then he returned to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of that, and he said: "That was al-ʿUzza, and she will never be worshipped again." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/100.]] [129]

Al-Dahhak said: It was an idol of Ghatafan, which Saʿd ibn Zalim al-Ghatafani set up for them. He came to Mecca and saw al-Safa and al-Marwah, and saw the people of Mecca going around between them. He returned to [Batn Nakhlah] and said to his people:

"The people of Mecca have al-Safa and al-Marwah and you do not have them, and they have a god they worship and you do not have one." They said: "What do you command us?" He said: "I will make for you the same." He took a stone from al-Safa and a stone from al-Marwah, and carried them to Batn Nakhlah. He placed the one from al-Safa and said: "This is al-Safa," then he placed the one he had taken from al-Marwah and said: "This is al-Marwah." Then he took three stones and leaned them against a tree and said: "This is your lord." They began to go around between the two stones and worship the stones, until the Messenger of Allah conquered Mecca, and he ordered the stones removed, and sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to al-ʿUzza, and he cut them down.

Ibn Zayd said: It was a house at al-Ta'if which Thaqif worshipped.

Wa-manāt: Ibn Kathir read it with a long vowel (al-madd), and similarly al-Shammuni narrated from Abu Bakr from ʿAsim, and recited:

"Has there not reached the Taym ibn ʿAbd Manat, against the Shanʾ, between us, Ibn Tamim?"

The rest read it short.

Qatadah said: It is stones that were worshipped. Ibn Zayd said: a house at al-Mushallal worshipped by the Banu Kaʿb.

Al-Dahhak said: Manat was an idol of Hudhayl and Khuza'ah, worshipped by the people of Mecca. It was also said that its etymology is from nā' al-najm yanūʾ nawʾan (the rising of the star). Some said: al-Lat, al-ʿUzza and Manat are idols of stone which were inside the Ka'bah, and they worshipped them.

The readers differed over stopping on al-Lat and Manat: some stopped on them with a hā', and some with a tā'. Some said: Everything in the Qur'an written with a tā' is stopped on with a tā', such as bi-niʿmati rabbika and shajarat al-zaqqum and the like; and whatever is written with a hā', stopping on it is with a hā'. Others said: The preference in every word that is not in construct (idafah) is to be with a hā', like raḥmatun min rabbī and shajaratan takhruju; and whatever is in construct is permissible with a hā' or a tā': the tā' for the construct and the hā' because it is standing alone without the tā'.

As for His saying, the Third, the Other (al-thālithata al-ukhrā): the Arabs do not say "the third, other" (al-thālithah ukhrā); rather "ukhrā" is an adjective of the second. The scholars differed about its explanation. Al-Khalil said: He only said that to match the endings of the verses, like His saying: ﴿needs (maʾārib) other﴾, and He did not say "akhar." Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: There is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir) in the verse; its meaning is: "Have you considered al-Lat and al-ʿUzza the other, and Manat the third?" The meaning of the verse: "Have you considered, O you who claim that al-Lat, al-ʿUzza and Manat are daughters of Allah,"

﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him? That is then an unjust division.﴾ Ibn Kathir's transmitters al-Qawwas and al-Bazzi read it with hamzah (ḍi'zā); the rest without hamzah. Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said: that is, an unjust division, since you assigned to your Lord what you dislike for yourselves. Mujahid and Muqatil: crooked. Al-Hasan: not balanced. Ibn Sirin: not equal, that they should have males and Allah should have females. Al-Dahhak: deficient. Sufyan: diminished. Ibn Zayd: contrary.

Al-Kisa'i said: It is said: ḍāza yaḍīzu ḍayzan; ḍāza yaḍūzu ḍawzan; ḍāza yuḍāzu ḍa'zan, meaning he wronged and diminished. A poet said:

"The Banu Asad were wronged in their judgment, when they made the head like the tail."

Al-Akhfash recited:

"If you withdraw from us, we shall diminish you; and if you are absent, your arrow is unfit and your nose is humbled."

The form ḍīzā in terms of grammar is fu'lā with the fa' pronounced with a ḍammah, because it is an adjective, and adjectives are only fu'lā with a ḍammah, such as ḥublā, unthā and yusrā; or fa'lā with a fatḥah, such as ghaḍbā, sakrā and ʿaṭshā. There is no fu'lā with a kasrah in the fa' among adjectives in Arabic; it occurs only in nouns, such as difrā, dhikrā and shi'rā. The historian said: They disliked the ḍammah on the ḍād and feared the ya' turning into waw, and it comes from the ya' roots, so they gave the ḍād a kasrah for this reason, as they said for the plural of abyad: bīḍ, the original being buwḍ, like ḥumr and ṣafr. As for the one who said ḍāza yaḍūzu, its noun is ḍawzā, like shawrā.

Inna hiya, meaning these idols, illā asmā'un sammaytumūhā antum wa-ābā'ukum mā anzala Allāhu bihā min sulṭān (They are only names which you and your fathers have named; Allah has sent down no authority for them). The common reading is with yā' (in yattabiʿūna); ʿIsa read it with tā'. Illā al-ẓanna (except conjecture) in their saying that they are gods and that they are their intercessors, wa-mā tahwā al-anfusu (and what the souls desire). And He has certainly sent them guidance from their Lord, to show that they are not gods, and that worship is fit only for Allah, the One, the Subduer.

And He certainly saw him another time, a second descent (nazlah ukhra), and He called it a "descent" by way of metaphor. This is because Jibril (Gabriel) was seen by the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) in the form in which he was created, twice: once at the highest horizon on earth, and once near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha) in the heavens. This is the view of ʿĀ'ishah and most of the scholars, and it is the preferred one, because He linked the seeing with a place when He said ʿinda sidrat al-muntahā, and because He said nazlatan ukhrā, whose implied meaning is: "He saw him descending another time." Attributing place and descent, which is movement, to God is impossible. Also, He said nazlatan ukhrā, and it is not reported in any hadith that the Prophet ﷺ saw his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, before the night of the Ascension (mi'raj) and then saw Him again that night. What supports this is:

ʿaqil ibn Muhammad informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: ʿAbd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, who said: Dawud ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, from Masruq, that ʿĀ'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has greatly slandered Allah."

He said: I was reclining, so I sat up and said: "O Mother of the Believers, grant me a moment and do not hurry. Tell me about the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And he certainly saw him another time﴾ and ﴿And he certainly saw him at the clear horizon﴾." She said: "It was only Jibril. He saw him in his form in which he was created, twice: once when he descended from the sky to the earth, filling the greatest span between the sky and the earth, and once near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary." She said: "And I was the first to ask the Prophet about this verse, and he said: 'It is Jibril.'" [124]

ʿinda sidrat al-muntahā: ʿinda is connected to his saying ra'āhu (he saw him). The sidrah is the lote-tree (shajrat al-nabiq). It was called "the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary" because the knowledge of every knower ends at it.

Hilal ibn Sayyaf said: Ibn ʿAbbas asked Kaʿb about the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary while I was present, and Kaʿb said: "It is a lote-tree at the base of the Throne, on the heads of the bearers of the Throne, and the knowledge of creation ends at it, and what lies beyond it is unseen, which none knows except Allah, the Glorified."

Ibn Masʿud said: it was named so because what descends from above it and what ascends from below it, of the command of Allah, the Exalted, ends at it. When one who ascends to it from the earth reaches it, it is seized from it. It was also said: it is because the spirits of believers ascend and end at it. And it was said: it is because everyone who dies upon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah and his way ends at it.

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu al-ʿĀliyah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey (usriya bihi), he reached the Lote-tree, and it was said to him: "This is the Lote-tree, to which every one of your community who follows your Sunnah will come." Behold, from its root flow rivers of water unaltered (ghayru asin) up to His saying: "purified" (muṣaffā). It is a tree under whose shade a rider travels for seventy years without crossing it, and one of its leaves covers the whole community.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shaybah narrated to us, who said: al-Tanukhi narrated to us, who said: ʿUbayd ibn Yaʿish narrated to us, who said: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, from Yahya ibn ʿAbbad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from his grandmother Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ mention the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, and he said:

"A rider travels in the shade of its branch for a hundred years, and a hundred riders can take shelter in its branches. In it are golden butterflies, and its fruits are like jars (qilal)." [125] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/86, with slight variation]]

Muqatil said: It is a tree such that if one of its leaves were placed on the earth, it would light up for the people of the earth; it bears ornaments, garments and fruits of every colour. And if a man were to ride a swift she-camel and go around its trunk, he would not reach the place from which he set out until old age killed him. It is the Tuba (ṭūbā) which Allah mentioned in Surat al-Raʿd. I have fully described its attributes in the account of the Night Journey.

ʿindahā jannat al-maʾwā, idh yaghshā al-sidrata mā yaghshā (Near it is the Garden of Refuge, when there covers the Lote-tree what covers).

Ibn Masʿud and his companions said: "Golden butterflies." This is also the narration of al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas, and he traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ.

Al-Hasan said: The light of the Lord of Majesty covered it and it became radiant. It was also said: the angels.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw on every leaf of it an angel standing, glorifying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [126]

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu Hurayrah or another, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote-tree. He said: The light of creation covered it, and the angels covered it out of love for Allah, like crows when they alight on a tree.

He said: Then He spoke to him at that moment and said: "Ask."

In a hadith: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Then there covered it [in the source: yaghshāhā] a fluttering of green birds." [127] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/97.]]

Al-Suddi said: "Of birds, above it."

Anas narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I reached the Lote-tree, and I knew that it was the Lote-tree; I know its leaves and its fruit, and when its ripe fruit is like jars, and its leaves like elephants' ears. When there covered it of the command of Allah what covered it, it turned into rubies and emeralds, until no one can describe it. Near it is the Garden of Refuge." [128] [[See Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/72071; the hadith is not one single report.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is the right side of the Throne, and it is the station of the martyrs, like His saying: ﴿For them are the Gardens of Refuge﴾.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbd Allah ʿUmar ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Harith al-Qadibani narrated to us. He said: ʿAli ibn al-ʿAbbas al-Muqanaʿi narrated to us, who said: Maymun ibn al-Asbaʿ narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Salih al-Wuhadhi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Hamzah al-Basri narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr recite this verse as ʿindahā jannah (with a hā' at the end), meaning "the garden of spending the night" (jannat al-mabit).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and ʿUbayd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid narrated to us, who said: Abu Sadaqah narrated to me, who said: Abu al-Asbat narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, from ʿAli ibn al-Qasim al-Kindi, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi recite jannah al-maʾwā (with a hā'). Mujahid said: he means ajannahu (He covered him), and the hā' in this reading refers to the Prophet ﷺ.

Abu Hatim said: This is the reading of ʿAli and Anas, meaning "covered him." Al-Akhfash said: "reached him" (adrakahu).

Mā zāgha al-baṣaru wa-mā ṭagha (His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress): that is, he did not go beyond what he was commanded, nor did he turn away from what he was sent to see.

Laqad raʾā min āyāti rabbihi al-kubrā (He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord): that is, the greatest sign.

Ibn Masʿud said: He saw a green fluttering from Paradise that filled the horizon. Al-Dahhak said: the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He saw Jibril in his form which he has in the heavens. It was also said: the Ascension (al-miʿraj), and what was shown to him that night in his journey and his return and his beginning. The proof is His saying: ﴿So that We may show you of Our greatest signs﴾ ...

Afa-ra'aytumu al-lāt (Have you considered al-Lat?). The common reading is with the tā' lightened. It is derived from (Allah), and a tā' was added to it, so it became feminine. Just as it is said ʿumar for the male, then ʿumrah for the female, and ʿabbās and ʿabbāsah. When he died, they devoted themselves to his grave and worshipped him. Mujahid said: He was a man on the top of a mountain who had goats from which he would collect butter and take aqit (dried curd), and gather their milk, and then prepare from it hays (a mixture of dates, aqit and ghee) which he fed to the pilgrims. Al-Kalbi said: He was a man from Thaqif called Sakhrah ibn Ghanm, who used to melt butter and place it on a rock, and the Arabs would come and smear their swords with it. When the man died, Thaqif took the rock to their dwellings and worshipped it; the idol of al-Ta'if was based on the placing of al-Lat.

Wal-ʿUzzā: they differed about it. Mujahid said: It is a tree belonging to Ghatafan, which they worshipped.

It was this that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Khalid ibn al-Walid against, and he cut it down, and Khalid began striking it with an axe, saying:

"O ʿUzza, disbelief in you! No glory to you! Indeed I have seen that Allah has humiliated you."

From it there came out a female devil, with hair flowing and crying out woe, placing her hand on her head. It is said that Khalid returned to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "I have cut it down." He said: "What did you see?" He said: "I saw nothing." He said: "You have not cut it." So he went back to it with the axe, uprooted it and pulled out its root, and out came a naked woman, and he killed her. Then he returned to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of that, and he said: "That was al-ʿUzza, and she will never be worshipped again." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/100.]] [129]

Al-Dahhak said: It was an idol of Ghatafan, which Saʿd ibn Zalim al-Ghatafani set up for them. He came to Mecca and saw al-Safa and al-Marwah, and saw the people of Mecca going around between them. He returned to [Batn Nakhlah] and said to his people:

"The people of Mecca have al-Safa and al-Marwah and you do not have them, and they have a god they worship and you do not have one." They said: "What do you command us?" He said: "I will make for you the same." He took a stone from al-Safa and a stone from al-Marwah, and carried them to Batn Nakhlah. He placed the one from al-Safa and said: "This is al-Safa," then he placed the one he had taken from al-Marwah and said: "This is al-Marwah." Then he took three stones and leaned them against a tree and said: "This is your lord." They began to go around between the two stones and worship the stones, until the Messenger of Allah conquered Mecca, and he ordered the stones removed, and sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to al-ʿUzza, and he cut them down.

Ibn Zayd said: It was a house at al-Ta'if which Thaqif worshipped.

"Has there not reached the Taym ibn ʿAbd Manat, against the Shanʾ, between us, Ibn Tamim?"

The rest read it short.

The scholars differed about its explanation. Al-Khalil said: He only said that to match the endings of the verses, like His saying: ﴿needs (maʾārib) other﴾, and He did not say "akhar." Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: There is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir) in the verse; its meaning is: "Have you considered al-Lat and al-ʿUzza the other, and Manat the third?" The meaning of the verse: "Have you considered, O you who claim that al-Lat, al-ʿUzza and Manat are daughters of Allah,"

﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him? That is then an unjust division.﴾ Ibn Kathir's transmitters al-Qawwas and al-Bazzi read it with hamzah (ḍi'zā); the rest without hamzah. Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said: that is, an unjust division, since you assigned to your Lord what you dislike for yourselves. Mujahid and Muqatil: crooked. Al-Hasan: not balanced. Ibn Sirin: not equal, that they should have males and Allah should have females. Al-Dahhak: deficient. Sufyan: diminished. Ibn Zayd: contrary.

Al-Kisa'i said: It is said: ḍāza yaḍīzu ḍayzan; ḍāza yaḍūzu ḍawzan; ḍāza yuḍāzu ḍa'zan, meaning he wronged and diminished. A poet said:

"The Banu Asad were wronged in their judgment, when they made the head like the tail."

Al-Akhfash recited:

"If you withdraw from us, we shall diminish you; and if you are absent, your arrow is unfit and your nose is humbled."

There is no fu'lā with a kasrah in the fa' among adjectives in Arabic; it occurs only in nouns, such as difrā, dhikrā and shi'rā. The historian said: They disliked the ḍammah on the ḍād and feared the ya' turning into waw, and it comes from the ya' roots, so they gave the ḍād a kasrah for this reason, as they said for the plural of abyad: bīḍ, the original being buwḍ, like ḥumr and ṣafr. As for the one who said ḍāza yaḍūzu, its noun is ḍawzā, like shawrā.

Inna hiya, meaning these idols, illā asmā'un sammaytumūhā antum wa-ābā'ukum mā anzala Allāhu bihā min sulṭān (They are only names which you and your fathers have named; Allah has sent down no authority for them). The common reading is with yā' (in yattabiʿūna); ʿIsa read it with tā'. Illā al-ẓanna (except conjecture) in their saying that they are gods and that they are their intercessors, wa-mā tahwā al-anfusu (and what the souls desire). And He has certainly sent them guidance from their Lord, to show that they are not gods, and that worship is fit only for Allah, the One, the Subduer.

And He certainly saw him another time, a second descent (nazlah ukhra), and He called it a "descent" by way of metaphor. This is because Jibril (Gabriel) was seen by the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) in the form in which he was created, twice: once at the highest horizon on earth, and once near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha) in the heavens. This is the view of ʿĀ'ishah and most of the scholars, and it is the preferred one, because He linked the seeing with a place when He said ʿinda sidrat al-muntahā, and because He said nazlatan ukhrā, whose implied meaning is: "He saw him descending another time." Attributing place and descent, which is movement, to God is impossible. Also, He said nazlatan ukhrā, and it is not reported in any hadith that the Prophet ﷺ saw his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, before the night of the Ascension (mi'raj) and then saw Him again that night. What supports this is:

ʿaqil ibn Muhammad informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: ʿAbd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, who said: Dawud ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, from Masruq, that ʿĀ'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has greatly slandered Allah."

He said: I was reclining, so I sat up and said: "O Mother of the Believers, grant me a moment and do not hurry. Tell me about the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And he certainly saw him another time﴾ and ﴿And he certainly saw him at the clear horizon﴾." She said: "It was only Jibril. He saw him in his form in which he was created, twice: once when he descended from the sky to the earth, filling the greatest span between the sky and the earth, and once near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary." She said: "And I was the first to ask the Prophet about this verse, and he said: 'It is Jibril.'" [124]

ʿinda sidrat al-muntahā: ʿinda is connected to his saying ra'āhu (he saw him). The sidrah is the lote-tree (shajrat al-nabiq). It was called "the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary" because the knowledge of every knower ends at it.

Hilal ibn Sayyaf said: Ibn ʿAbbas asked Kaʿb about the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary while I was present, and Kaʿb said: "It is a lote-tree at the base of the Throne, on the heads of the bearers of the Throne, and the knowledge of creation ends at it, and what lies beyond it is unseen, which none knows except Allah, the Glorified."

Ibn Masʿud said: it was named so because what descends from above it and what ascends from below it, of the command of Allah, the Exalted, ends at it. When one who ascends to it from the earth reaches it, it is seized from it. It was also said: it is because the spirits of believers ascend and end at it. And it was said: it is because everyone who dies upon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah and his way ends at it.

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu al-ʿĀliyah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey (usriya bihi), he reached the Lote-tree, and it was said to him: "This is the Lote-tree, to which every one of your community who follows your Sunnah will come." Behold, from its root flow rivers of water unaltered (ghayru asin) up to His saying: "purified" (muṣaffā). It is a tree under whose shade a rider travels for seventy years without crossing it, and one of its leaves covers the whole community.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shaybah narrated to us, who said: al-Tanukhi narrated to us, who said: ʿUbayd ibn Yaʿish narrated to us, who said: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, from Yahya ibn ʿAbbad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from his grandmother Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ mention the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, and he said:

"A rider travels in the shade of its branch for a hundred years, and a hundred riders can take shelter in its branches. In it are golden butterflies, and its fruits are like jars (qilal)." [125] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/86, with slight variation]]

Muqatil said: It is a tree such that if one of its leaves were placed on the earth, it would light up for the people of the earth; it bears ornaments, garments and fruits of every colour. And if a man were to ride a swift she-camel and go around its trunk, he would not reach the place from which he set out until old age killed him. It is the Tuba (ṭūbā) which Allah mentioned in Surat al-Raʿd. I have fully described its attributes in the account of the Night Journey.

ʿindahā jannat al-maʾwā, idh yaghshā al-sidrata mā yaghshā (Near it is the Garden of Refuge, when there covers the Lote-tree what covers).

Ibn Masʿud and his companions said: "Golden butterflies." This is also the narration of al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas, and he traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ.

Al-Hasan said: The light of the Lord of Majesty covered it and it became radiant. It was also said: the angels.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw on every leaf of it an angel standing, glorifying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [126]

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu Hurayrah or another, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote-tree. He said: The light of creation covered it, and the angels covered it out of love for Allah, like crows when they alight on a tree.

He said: Then He spoke to him at that moment and said: "Ask."

In a hadith: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Then there covered it [in the source: yaghshāhā] a fluttering of green birds." [127] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/97.]]

Al-Suddi said: "Of birds, above it."

Anas narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I reached the Lote-tree, and I knew that it was the Lote-tree; I know its leaves and its fruit, and when its ripe fruit is like jars, and its leaves like elephants' ears. When there covered it of the command of Allah what covered it, it turned into rubies and emeralds, until no one can describe it. Near it is the Garden of Refuge." [128] [[See Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/72071; the hadith is not one single report.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is the right side of the Throne, and it is the station of the martyrs, like His saying: ﴿For them are the Gardens of Refuge﴾.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbd Allah ʿUmar ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Harith al-Qadibani narrated to us. He said: ʿAli ibn al-ʿAbbas al-Muqanaʿi narrated to us, who said: Maymun ibn al-Asbaʿ narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Salih al-Wuhadhi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Hamzah al-Basri narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr recite this verse as ʿindahā jannah (with a hā' at the end), meaning "the garden of spending the night" (jannat al-mabit).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and ʿUbayd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid narrated to us, who said: Abu Sadaqah narrated to me, who said: Abu al-Asbat narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, from ʿAli ibn al-Qasim al-Kindi, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi recite jannah al-maʾwā (with a hā'). Mujahid said: he means ajannahu (He covered him), and the hā' in this reading refers to the Prophet ﷺ.

Abu Hatim said: This is the reading of ʿAli and Anas, meaning "covered him." Al-Akhfash said: "reached him" (adrakahu).

Mā zāgha al-baṣaru wa-mā ṭagha (His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress): that is, he did not go beyond what he was commanded, nor did he turn away from what he was sent to see.

Laqad raʾā min āyāti rabbihi al-kubrā (He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord): that is, the greatest sign.

Ibn Masʿud said: He saw a green fluttering from Paradise that filled the horizon. Al-Dahhak said: the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He saw Jibril in his form which he has in the heavens. It was also said: the Ascension (al-miʿraj), and what was shown to him that night in his journey and his return and his beginning. The proof is His saying: ﴿So that We may show you of Our greatest signs﴾ ...

Afa-ra'aytumu al-lāt (Have you considered al-Lat?). The common reading is with the tā' lightened. It is derived from (Allah), and a tā' was added to it, so it became feminine. Just as it is said ʿumar for the male, then ʿumrah for the female, and ʿabbās and ʿabbāsah. Likewise the polytheists named their idols after the names of Allah: they said from Allah (al-Lāt), and from al-ʿAzīz (al-ʿUzzā).

Qatadah said: As for al-Lat, it was at al-Ta'if. Ibn Zayd said: al-Lat was a house at Nakhlah which Quraysh worshipped.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid and Abu Salih read al-Lāt with the tā' doubled, and they said: he was a man who used to pound (yaltu) sawiq for the pilgrims. When he died, they devoted themselves to his grave and worshipped him. Al-Suddi narrated from Abu Salih that he was at al-Ta'if, and he used to attend to their gods and pound sawiq for them; when he died, they worshipped him.

Mujahid said: He was a man on the top of a mountain who had goats from which he would collect butter and take aqit (dried curd), and gather their milk, and then prepare from it hays (a mixture of dates, aqit and ghee) which he fed to the pilgrims. He was at Batn Nakhlah, and when he died they worshipped him, and he is al-Lat. Al-Kalbi said: He was a man from Thaqif called Sakhrah ibn Ghanm, who used to melt butter and place it on a rock, and the Arabs would come and smear their swords with it. When the man died, Thaqif took the rock to their dwellings and worshipped it; the idol of al-Ta'if was based on the placing of al-Lat.

Wal-ʿUzzā: they differed about it. Mujahid said: It is a tree belonging to Ghatafan, which they worshipped.

It was this that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Khalid ibn al-Walid against, and he cut it down, and Khalid began striking it with an axe, saying:

"O ʿUzza, disbelief in you! No glory to you! Indeed I have seen that Allah has humiliated you."

From it there came out a female devil, with hair flowing and crying out woe, placing her hand on her head. It is said that Khalid returned to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "I have cut it down." He said: "What did you see?" He said: "I saw nothing." He said: "You have not cut it." So he went back to it with the axe, uprooted it and pulled out its root, and out came a naked woman, and he killed her. Then he returned to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of that, and he said: "That was al-ʿUzza, and she will never be worshipped again." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/100.]] [129]

Al-Dahhak said: It was an idol of Ghatafan, which Saʿd ibn Zalim al-Ghatafani set up for them. He came to Mecca and saw al-Safa and al-Marwah, and saw the people of Mecca going around between them. He returned to [Batn Nakhlah] and said to his people:

"The people of Mecca have al-Safa and al-Marwah and you do not have them, and they have a god they worship and you do not have one." They said: "What do you command us?" He said: "I will make for you the same." He took a stone from al-Safa and a stone from al-Marwah, and carried them to Batn Nakhlah. He placed the one from al-Safa and said: "This is al-Safa," then he placed the one he had taken from al-Marwah and said: "This is al-Marwah." Then he took three stones and leaned them against a tree and said: "This is your lord." They began to go around between the two stones and worship the stones, until the Messenger of Allah conquered Mecca, and he ordered the stones removed, and sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to al-ʿUzza, and he cut them down.

Ibn Zayd said: It was a house at al-Ta'if which Thaqif worshipped.

Wa-manāt: Ibn Kathir read it with a long vowel (al-madd), and similarly al-Shammuni narrated from Abu Bakr from ʿAsim, and recited:

"Has there not reached the Taym ibn ʿAbd Manat, against the Shanʾ, between us, Ibn Tamim?"

The rest read it short.

Qatadah said: It is stones that were worshipped. Ibn Zayd said: a house at al-Mushallal worshipped by the Banu Kaʿb.

Al-Dahhak said: Manat was an idol of Hudhayl and Khuza'ah, worshipped by the people of Mecca. It was also said that its etymology is from nā' al-najm yanūʾ nawʾan (the rising of the star). Some said: al-Lat, al-ʿUzza and Manat are idols of stone which were inside the Ka'bah, and they worshipped them.

The readers differed over stopping on al-Lat and Manat: some stopped on them with a hā', and some with a tā'. Some said: Everything in the Qur'an written with a tā' is stopped on with a tā', such as bi-niʿmati rabbika and shajarat al-zaqqum and the like; and whatever is written with a hā', stopping on it is with a hā'. Others said: The preference in every word that is not in construct (idafah) is to be with a hā', like raḥmatun min rabbī and shajaratan takhruju; and whatever is in construct is permissible with a hā' or a tā': the tā' for the construct and the hā' because it is standing alone without the tā'.

As for His saying, the Third, the Other (al-thālithata al-ukhrā): the Arabs do not say "the third, other" (al-thālithah ukhrā); rather "ukhrā" is an adjective of the second. The scholars differed about its explanation. Al-Khalil said: He only said that to match the endings of the verses, like His saying: ﴿needs (maʾārib) other﴾, and He did not say "akhar." Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: There is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir) in the verse; its meaning is: "Have you considered al-Lat and al-ʿUzza the other, and Manat the third?" The meaning of the verse: "Have you considered, O you who claim that al-Lat, al-ʿUzza and Manat are daughters of Allah,"

﴿Is the male for you and the female for Him? That is then an unjust division.﴾ Ibn Kathir's transmitters al-Qawwas and al-Bazzi read it with hamzah (ḍi'zā); the rest without hamzah. Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said: that is, an unjust division, since you assigned to your Lord what you dislike for yourselves. Mujahid and Muqatil: crooked. Al-Hasan: not balanced. Ibn Sirin: not equal, that they should have males and Allah should have females. Al-Dahhak: deficient. Sufyan: diminished. Ibn Zayd: contrary.

Al-Kisa'i said: It is said: ḍāza yaḍīzu ḍayzan; ḍāza yaḍūzu ḍawzan; ḍāza yuḍāzu ḍa'zan, meaning he wronged and diminished. A poet said:

"The Banu Asad were wronged in their judgment, when they made the head like the tail."

Al-Akhfash recited:

"If you withdraw from us, we shall diminish you; and if you are absent, your arrow is unfit and your nose is humbled."

The form ḍīzā in terms of grammar is fu'lā with the fa' pronounced with a ḍammah, because it is an adjective, and adjectives are only fu'lā with a ḍammah, such as ḥublā, unthā and yusrā; or fa'lā with a fatḥah, such as ghaḍbā, sakrā and ʿaṭshā. There is no fu'lā with a kasrah in the fa' among adjectives in Arabic; it occurs only in nouns, such as difrā, dhikrā and shi'rā. The historian said: They disliked the ḍammah on the ḍād and feared the ya' turning into waw, and it comes from the ya' roots, so they gave the ḍād a kasrah for this reason, as they said for the plural of abyad: bīḍ, the original being buwḍ, like ḥumr and ṣafr. As for the one who said ḍāza yaḍūzu, its noun is ḍawzā, like shawrā.

Inna hiya, meaning these idols, illā asmā'un sammaytumūhā antum wa-ābā'ukum mā anzala Allāhu bihā min sulṭān (They are only names which you and your fathers have named; Allah has sent down no authority for them). The common reading is with yā' (in yattabiʿūna); ʿIsa read it with tā'. Illā al-ẓanna (except conjecture) in their saying that they are gods and that they are their intercessors, wa-mā tahwā al-anfusu (and what the souls desire). And He has certainly sent them guidance from their Lord, to show that they are not gods, and that worship is fit only for Allah, the One, the Subduer.

And He certainly saw him another time, a second descent (nazlah ukhra), and He called it a "descent" by way of metaphor. This is because Jibril (Gabriel) was seen by the Prophet ﷺ (ﷺ) in the form in which he was created, twice: once at the highest horizon on earth, and once near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha) in the heavens. This is the view of ʿĀ'ishah and most of the scholars, and it is the preferred one, because He linked the seeing with a place when He said ʿinda sidrat al-muntahā, and because He said nazlatan ukhrā, whose implied meaning is: "He saw him descending another time." Attributing place and descent, which is movement, to God is impossible. Also, He said nazlatan ukhrā, and it is not reported in any hadith that the Prophet ﷺ saw his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, before the night of the Ascension (mi'raj) and then saw Him again that night. What supports this is:

ʿaqil ibn Muhammad informed me that Abu al-Faraj informed them, from Muhammad ibn Jarir, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: ʿAbd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi narrated to us, who said: Dawud ibn ʿAmir narrated to us, from Masruq, that ʿĀ'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord has greatly slandered Allah."

He said: I was reclining, so I sat up and said: "O Mother of the Believers, grant me a moment and do not hurry. Tell me about the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And he certainly saw him another time﴾ and ﴿And he certainly saw him at the clear horizon﴾." She said: "It was only Jibril. He saw him in his form in which he was created, twice: once when he descended from the sky to the earth, filling the greatest span between the sky and the earth, and once near the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary." She said: "And I was the first to ask the Prophet about this verse, and he said: 'It is Jibril.'" [124]

ʿinda sidrat al-muntahā: ʿinda is connected to his saying ra'āhu (he saw him). The sidrah is the lote-tree (shajrat al-nabiq). It was called "the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary" because the knowledge of every knower ends at it.

Hilal ibn Sayyaf said: Ibn ʿAbbas asked Kaʿb about the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary while I was present, and Kaʿb said: "It is a lote-tree at the base of the Throne, on the heads of the bearers of the Throne, and the knowledge of creation ends at it, and what lies beyond it is unseen, which none knows except Allah, the Glorified."

Ibn Masʿud said: it was named so because what descends from above it and what ascends from below it, of the command of Allah, the Exalted, ends at it. When one who ascends to it from the earth reaches it, it is seized from it. It was also said: it is because the spirits of believers ascend and end at it. And it was said: it is because everyone who dies upon the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah and his way ends at it.

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu al-ʿĀliyah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey (usriya bihi), he reached the Lote-tree, and it was said to him: "This is the Lote-tree, to which every one of your community who follows your Sunnah will come." Behold, from its root flow rivers of water unaltered (ghayru asin) up to His saying: "purified" (muṣaffā). It is a tree under whose shade a rider travels for seventy years without crossing it, and one of its leaves covers the whole community.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shaybah narrated to us, who said: al-Tanukhi narrated to us, who said: ʿUbayd ibn Yaʿish narrated to us, who said: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, from Yahya ibn ʿAbbad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from his grandmother Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ mention the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, and he said:

"A rider travels in the shade of its branch for a hundred years, and a hundred riders can take shelter in its branches. In it are golden butterflies, and its fruits are like jars (qilal)." [125] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 4/86, with slight variation]]

Muqatil said: It is a tree such that if one of its leaves were placed on the earth, it would light up for the people of the earth; it bears ornaments, garments and fruits of every colour. And if a man were to ride a swift she-camel and go around its trunk, he would not reach the place from which he set out until old age killed him. It is the Tuba (ṭūbā) which Allah mentioned in Surat al-Raʿd. I have fully described its attributes in the account of the Night Journey.

ʿindahā jannat al-maʾwā, idh yaghshā al-sidrata mā yaghshā (Near it is the Garden of Refuge, when there covers the Lote-tree what covers).

Ibn Masʿud and his companions said: "Golden butterflies." This is also the narration of al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas, and he traced it back to the Prophet ﷺ.

Al-Hasan said: The light of the Lord of Majesty covered it and it became radiant. It was also said: the angels.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I saw on every leaf of it an angel standing, glorifying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [126]

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu Hurayrah or another, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote-tree. He said: The light of creation covered it, and the angels covered it out of love for Allah, like crows when they alight on a tree.

He said: Then He spoke to him at that moment and said: "Ask."

In a hadith: the Prophet ﷺ said: "Then there covered it [in the source: yaghshāhā] a fluttering of green birds." [127] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/97.]]

Al-Suddi said: "Of birds, above it."

Anas narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I reached the Lote-tree, and I knew that it was the Lote-tree; I know its leaves and its fruit, and when its ripe fruit is like jars, and its leaves like elephants' ears. When there covered it of the command of Allah what covered it, it turned into rubies and emeralds, until no one can describe it. Near it is the Garden of Refuge." [128] [[See Jami al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 27/72071; the hadith is not one single report.]]

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is the right side of the Throne, and it is the station of the martyrs, like His saying: ﴿For them are the Gardens of Refuge﴾.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbd Allah ʿUmar ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Harith al-Qadibani narrated to us. He said: ʿAli ibn al-ʿAbbas al-Muqanaʿi narrated to us, who said: Maymun ibn al-Asbaʿ narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Salih al-Wuhadhi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Hamzah al-Basri narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr recite this verse as ʿindahā jannah (with a hā' at the end), meaning "the garden of spending the night" (jannat al-mabit).

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Talhah ibn Muhammad and ʿUbayd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to us, both saying: Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid narrated to us, who said: Abu Sadaqah narrated to me, who said: Abu al-Asbat narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, from ʿAli ibn al-Qasim al-Kindi, from Musa ibn ʿUbaydah, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi recite jannah al-maʾwā (with a hā'). Mujahid said: he means ajannahu (He covered him), and the hā' in this reading refers to the Prophet ﷺ.

Abu Hatim said: This is the reading of ʿAli and Anas, meaning "covered him." Al-Akhfash said: "reached him" (adrakahu).

Mā zāgha al-baṣaru wa-mā ṭagha (His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress): that is, he did not go beyond what he was commanded, nor did he turn away from what he was sent to see.

Laqad raʾā min āyāti rabbihi al-kubrā (He certainly saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord): that is, the greatest sign.

Ibn Masʿud said: He saw a green fluttering from Paradise that filled the horizon. Al-Dahhak said: the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary. ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Yazid and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He saw Jibril in his form which he has in the heavens. It was also said: the Ascension (al-miʿraj), and what was shown to him that night in his journey and his return and his beginning. **Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 53, verses 24–32:**

Am lil-insani ma tamanna (Or does man have whatever he wishes?) — "ishtahā" (he desires). They are the disbelievers, who claimed that the idols would intercede for them with God. The meaning: do you suppose that they will have what they wish of intercession by the idols? It is not as they supposed or wished. Rather, to God belong "al-ākhira wa'l-ūlā" (the Hereafter and the former), meaning the world (al-dunya). He gives what He wills and withholds what He wills, not what man wishes and desires. This is like His saying: ﴿Is there a god with God?﴾, meaning there is no god with God. Ibn Zayd said: If Muhammad wished for something and God gave him that, then do not deny it.

﴿So to God belong the Hereafter and the former. He gives to whom He wills what He wills, and withholds from whom He wills what He wills.﴾

Al-Farra' said: lamam is what is close to minor sins; the root of lamam and ilmam is what a person does time after time, and from time to time, and does not go deep into it or persist in it. It is said: "alamtu bihi" when I visited him and departed, like the "ilmam" of a phantom. Al-A'sha said:

"A phantom of Qutaylah came by after
she and our rope had been severed."

Another said:

"When the phantom of you came visiting at night, its wandering for you is a reminder and a passion."

﴿Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness﴾; no sin overwhelms Him. Its parallel is: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us, saying: Abu 'Abdullah Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man ibn 'Abd al-Salam al-Isfahani related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Asim related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, saying: al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Wa'il, who said: Abu Musayrah 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, who was among the distinguished companions of 'Abdullah, saw in a dream: "I dreamt that I entered Paradise, and behold, there were pavilions erected. I said: 'For whom are these?' They said: 'For Dhu'l-Kala' and Hawshab' — and both were among those who were killed with Mu'awiyah. I said: 'Where are 'Ammar and his companions?' They said: 'Ahead of you.' I said: 'And some of them had killed others?' They said: 'They met God, and found Him vast in forgiveness.'"

Abu Khalid said: It has reached me that Dhu'l-Kala' freed twelve thousand slave girls.

﴿He knows you best, since He produced you from the earth﴾, meaning He created your father from dust, ﴿and when you were embryos (ajinnah)﴾, plural of janin, which is the child as long as it is in the womb; it is called janin because it is concealed (ijtinan), i.e., hidden.

Masruq narrated from 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: When a friend of the Jews died, they would say: "He is a saint."

This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "They lie. No soul that God creates in its mother's womb is anything but wretched or happy."[132] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 1/122.]] Then God revealed: ﴿He knows you best, since He produced you from the earth and when you were embryos.﴾

﴿In the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim your own purity.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not praise them. Mujahid and Zayd ibn Aslam: do not absolve them. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: some people would do evil deeds and then say: "Our prayer, our fasting, and our pilgrimage." So God revealed this.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When you see those who praise excessively, throw dust in their faces."[133] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/94.]]

﴿He knows best who is mindful of God﴾, i.e., who avoided shirk and believed.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God honour his face, said: it means one who does a good deed and refrains from an evil one. Al-Hasan said: one who makes his deed sincere for God.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 53, verse 33–44:

﴿Have you seen the one who turned away...﴾ ... the verses. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and al-Musayyib ibn Sharik said: it was revealed concerning 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, who used to give charity and spend in good causes. His foster brother 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Sarh said to him: "What is this that you are doing? Soon nothing will be left for you." 'Uthman said: "I have sins and wrongdoings, and by what I do I seek the pleasure of Allah and hope for His pardon." 'Abd Allah said to him: "Give me your she-camel with its saddle, and I will bear all your sins for you." So he gave it to him, and had him testify to it, and refrained from some of the charity and spending he had been doing. Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾, meaning on the day of Uhud, when he abandoned his position [[Meaning: when he abandoned the position in the battle.]].

﴿And gave a little and then withheld﴾, meaning his companion gave a little and then cut off his spending. 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, then returned to the best and finest of that (course).

Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. He had followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his religion, but some of the polytheists reproached him and said: "Have you abandoned the religion of the elders, misled them, and claimed that they are in the Fire? You should have supported them." He said: "I feared the punishment of Allah." So the one who reproached him guaranteed to him that, if he gave him some of his wealth and returned to his polytheism, he would bear the punishment of Allah for him. He did so, and gave the one who had reproached him some of what he had guaranteed, then he became miserly and withheld the rest of what he had guaranteed.

So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾, meaning turned back from faith, ﴿and gave a little﴾, meaning his companion, the guarantor, ﴿and then withheld﴾, meaning he withheld the remainder. Muqatil said: it means al-Walid gave a little good with his tongue, then ﴿withheld﴾, that is, cut it off and did not persist in it.

Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Zubaydi related from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: it was revealed concerning a man who said to his family: "Equip me, I will go to this man," meaning the Prophet ﷺ. So he equipped himself and set out, and a man from among the disbelievers met him and said: "Where are you going?" He said: "To Muhammad, perhaps I will obtain some of his goodness." The man said to him: "Give me your equipment and I will bear your sin," and this verse was revealed concerning him.

It is also related from al-Suddi that he said: it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, because he would sometimes agree with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in some matters. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, because he said: "By Allah, Muhammad only orders us to the noble qualities of character." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿gave a little and then withheld﴾, that is, he did not believe.

The exegetes said: ﴿akda﴾ means he cut it off and did not persist in it, and its origin is from al-kudya, which is a rock that appears in a well and prevents digging and makes one despair of water.

Al-Kisa'i said: the Arabs say: "akda al-hafir" and "ajbal" when the digger reaches the kudya and the mountain (rock) in digging. He also said: "kadat asabi'uhu" when they became callused, and "kadat yaduhu" when it became weary and it did nothing, and "kadā al-nabt" when its growth diminished. The historian said: ﴿akda﴾ means he withheld good. Al-Hutay'a said:

He gave a little, then withheld his gift,
and whoever gives kindness among people is praised. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/112.]]

﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees? Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Musa﴾, meaning the books of the Torah, ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾, meaning what he was sent with of conveying the message of Allah, which is His saying: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾. Ikrima and Tawus related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: before Ibrahim, peace be upon him, they used to seize a man for the sin of another, and a guardian would be seized for a guardian in killing, so that a man would be killed for his father, his brother, his son, his paternal uncle, or his maternal uncle, a husband would be killed for his wife, and a master would be killed for his slave. Then came Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he forbade them from that and conveyed to them from Allah: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾.

Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: he acted upon what he was commanded and conveyed the messages of his Lord to His creation. Mujahid said: he fulfilled what was obligated upon him. Al-Rabi': he fulfilled his vision and carried out the slaughter of his son. 'Ata' al-Khurasani: he practised obedience. Abu al-'Aliya: he fulfilled the completeness of Islam, which is His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾, and no one was tested with this religion and fulfilled all its requirements except Ibrahim. The meaning of tawfiya is completion; one says: "I fulfilled his right to him and gave it in full," and Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿that He may pay them their rewards in full﴾. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna: he discharged the trust. Al-Dahhak: he fulfilled the matter of the rites. 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib: it has reached me that Ibrahim had made a pledge not to ask anything of a created being; when he was thrown into the Fire, Jibril came to him and said: "Do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no." So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, praised him for standing by what he said and fulfilling what he had pledged, so the Mighty One said: ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: he fulfilled the matter of guests, until he was named the father of guests. Abu Bakr al-Warraq: he upheld the condition of what he claimed, because Allah, glorified is He, said to him: "Submit," and he said: "I have submitted," so Allah, glorified is He, demanded the truth of his claim, and tested him in his wealth, his children and himself, and found him fulfilling all of that. So He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾, meaning he claimed Islam, then confirmed his claim.

It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ regarding the interpretation of this verse two statements:

The first: what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: al-Qati'i told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told me, saying: Husayn told us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a told us, saying: Rayyan ibn Fa'id told us, from Sahl, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Shall I not inform you why the Exalted named Ibrahim His friend, the one who fulfilled? Because he used to say every morning and evening: ﴿Glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ until he completed the verse." [134] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 1/735.]]

The second: what

al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Maqri told us, saying: Abu 'Umar told us, saying: Nasr ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Ma'mar ibn Sulayman informed us, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, that the Prophet ﷺ recited ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾ and said:

"Do you know with what he fulfilled?" [135] They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "He fulfilled it, meaning he performed four rak'as at the beginning of his day," which he would pray from the start of the day. [136]

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, saying: Mu'awiya told us, from Abu al-Zahiriya, from Kathir ibn Murra, from Nu'aym ibn Hammar, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah the Exalted says: O son of Adam, do not fall short of four rak'as at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you for its end." [137]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Samura told us, saying: Abu Talha Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Karim told us, saying: Nasr ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mu'tasim Abu Jamil told us, from Abu Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he recited "wa-Ibrahim alladhi wafa" lightly (with a light pronunciation).

As for the reconciliation between His saying: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾ and His saying: ﴿and they will surely bear their burdens and other burdens along with their burdens﴾, it is what al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: ﴿and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾ voluntarily, and ﴿they will surely bear their burdens and other burdens along with their burdens﴾ by compulsion.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Hulwani told us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Iyad ibn Laqit told us, from Abu Ramtha, who said: I went with my father to the Prophet ﷺ. When I saw him, my father said to me: "Do you know who this is? This is the Messenger of Allah." He said: I shuddered at what he said to me, for I had thought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was something unlike people, but he was a man with abundant hair, with traces of henna on it, and he wore two green garments. My father greeted him, then we sat and talked for a while. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to my father: "Is this your son?" My father said: "By the Lord of the Ka'ba, truly, I testify to it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled, laughing at the affirmation of my resemblance to my father and at my father's oath concerning me. He said: "Indeed, he will not commit a crime against you, nor will you against him," then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾. Then my father looked at a growth like a lump between his shoulders and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a physician of men; shall I treat it for you?" He said: "No, its physician is the One who created it." [138] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 13/337; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/279.]]

﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾, meaning what he works. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: this verse is abrogated, and then Allah revealed after it: ﴿And those who believed, and whose descendants followed them in faith — We will join them with their descendants﴾, and We did not deprive them of anything, so the children enter Paradise through the righteousness of their fathers.

Ikrima said: that applied to the people of Ibrahim and Musa; as for this nation, they have what they strive for and what others strive for. [Like] the good report of Sa'd when he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Will it benefit my mother if I give charity on her behalf?" He said: "Yes" [139], and the report of the woman who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "My father died without performing Hajj." He said: "Perform Hajj on his behalf." [140]

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿And that man will have nothing﴾ means the disbeliever; as for the believer, he has what he strove for and what was striven for on his behalf. It was also said: the disbeliever has no good except what he did, for which he is rewarded in the abode of this world, so that no good remains for him in the Hereafter.

It is related that 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had given al-'Abbas a shirt, which he had dressed him in. When 'Abd Allah died, the Messenger of Allah sent his shirt so that he might be shrouded in it. Thus no good deed remained for him in the Hereafter for which he would be rewarded.

I heard Ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Mudarib say: I heard my father say: 'Abd Allah ibn Tahir, governor of Khurasan, summoned al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl and said: "Three verses have become unclear to me, so I called you to clarify them for me." He said: "What are they, O Amir?" He said: Allah's saying regarding the two sons of Adam: ﴿and he became one of the regretful﴾; and the report that is authentic: "Regret is repentance"; [141] and His saying: ﴿every day He is in a matter﴾; and the authentic report: "The pen has dried with what is to happen until the Day of Resurrection" [142]; and His saying: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾. So what is the matter with the contradictions? Al-Husayn said: It is possible that Qabil's regret was not repentance for him, while the regret of this nation is repentance for it, since Allah, glorified is He, has singled out this nation with distinctions which other nations did not share.

There is another statement: that Qabil's regret was not over killing Habil, but over carrying him. As for His saying: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾, it means by way of justice; and the sense of the verse is: "And that man will have nothing except what he strives for, justly, [and I may reward him with one thousand for one as a bounty]." As for His saying: ﴿every day He is in a matter﴾, it refers to affairs He renews, not affairs He initiates; and the sense of the verse is driving the decrees toward their appointed times. He said: Then 'Abd Allah ibn Tahir stood up, kissed his head, and granted him his revenue.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: ﴿illa ma sa'a﴾ means "intended" (nawa). Its clarification is the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "People will be resurrected according to their intentions." [143] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1414; Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/419, no. 7242.]]

﴿And that his effort will be seen; then he will be given the fullest recompense﴾. Al-Akhfash said: one says "jazaytuhu al-jaza'" and "jazaytuhu bil-jaza'", there is no difference between them. A poet said:

If I repay 'Alqama ibn Sa'd for his effort,
I would not repay him with the trial of a single day. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/115.]]

So he combined the two dialects.

﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾, meaning the end of creation and their return; He is the one who recompenses them for their deeds. It was also said: from Him is the beginning of bounty, and to Him is the end of hopes.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sufyani informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sama' ibn Fath al-Hanbali told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Misri told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Mansur al-Sa'di told us, saying: al-'Abbas ibn Zafar told us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ, regarding His saying: ﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾, he said: "There is no reflection upon Allah." [144] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/696.]]

Evidence for this report is what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba told us, saying: 'Umayr ibn Mirdas told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Sulami told us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a told us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Sinan ibn Sa'd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is mentioned, then desist." [145] [[Musnad al-Shamiyin: 3/308, no. 2350.]]

[Akhbarana] Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Jamshadhi, by recitation, in the year 387, said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Majbur told us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya told me, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Junayd told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Mughanni told me, saying: Dawud, the paternal uncle of al-Husayn ibn Qabil, told us, from Qatada, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to his companions while they were reflecting, and he said: "What are you about?" They said: "We are reflecting upon the Creator." He said: "Reflect upon creation, and do not reflect upon the Creator, for thought cannot encompass Him. Reflect that Allah created the seven heavens and earths: the thickness of each earth is five hundred years, the distance between each two earths is five hundred years, the distance between the sky and the earth is five hundred years, the thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and the distance between each two heavens is five hundred years; and in the seventh heaven is a sea whose depth is equal to all of that, in which is an angel whose ankles do not reach the water." [146] [[The beginning of the hadith is in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/314; its end is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 28/195.]]

﴿And that He is the One who makes laugh and makes weep﴾, among His creation whomever He wills.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, saying: Dallal, daughter of Abu al-Mudall, told us, saying: al-Sahba' told us, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by some people who were laughing, and he said: "If you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little." [147] Then Jibril came down to him and said: "Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And that He is the One who makes laugh and weep﴾." So he returned to them and said: "I had not taken forty steps before Jibril came and said: Go to these people and tell them: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: He makes laugh and makes weep." [148] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/116.]]

'Ata' ibn Abi Aslam said: it means: He makes joyful and makes sad, because joy brings laughter and sorrow brings weeping.

I heard Abu Mansur al-Hamsadhi say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Razi say: I heard Yusuf ibn Jubayr say: Tahir al-Maqdisi was asked: "Do the angels laugh?" He said: "Nothing has laughed beneath the Throne since Hell was created." It was said to 'Umar: "Did the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, and faith was more firmly fixed in their hearts than the firm mountains." Mujahid said: He makes the people of Paradise laugh in Paradise, and makes the people of the Fire weep in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: He makes the earth laugh with vegetation and makes the sky weep with rain. It was also said: He makes the dawns laugh with lights and makes the sky weep with showers. Dhu al-Nun said: He makes the hearts of the believers and the knowers laugh with the sun of His recognition, and makes the hearts of the disbelieving and disobedient weep with the darkness of their denial and disobedience. Sahl: He makes the obedient laugh with mercy and makes the disobedient weep with wrath. Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi: He makes the believer laugh in the Hereafter and makes him weep in this world. Qassam ibn 'Abd Allah: He makes their teeth laugh and makes their hearts weep, and he recited in its meaning:

The tongue laughs while the entrails burn,
and its laughter is only falsehood and fabrication.
O Lord, a weeper with no tears in his eye,
and a laugher whose tooth has no strength left. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/117.]]

﴿And that He is the One who causes death and gives life﴾: He causes death, meaning He annihilates in this world, and gives life for resurrection. It was said: He causes the fathers to die and gives life to the sons. It was said: He causes the drop to die and gives life to the soul. It was said: He causes the disbeliever to die through denial and severance, and gives life to the believer through recognition and connection; He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life?﴾ Al-Qasim said: He causes to die regarding His remembrance and gives life through His remembrance. Ibn 'Ata': He causes death by His justice and gives life by His grace. It was said: He causes death by withholding and stinginess, and gives life by generosity and giving.

﴿Have you seen the one who turned away...﴾ ... the verses.
