[144] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/696.]]

Evidence for this report is what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba told us, saying: 'Umayr ibn Mirdas told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Sulami told us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a told us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Sinan ibn Sa'd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is mentioned, then desist." [145] [[Musnad al-Shamiyin: 3/308, no. 2350.]]

[Akhbarana] Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Jamshadhi, by recitation, in the year 387, said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Majbur told us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya told me, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Junayd told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Mughanni told me, saying: Dawud, the paternal uncle of al-Husayn ibn Qabil, told us, from Qatada, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to his companions while they were reflecting, and he said: "What are you about?" They said: "We are reflecting upon the Creator." He said: "Reflect upon creation, and do not reflect upon the Creator, for thought cannot encompass Him. Reflect that Allah created the seven heavens and earths: the thickness of each earth is five hundred years, the distance between each two earths is five hundred years, the distance between the sky and the earth is five hundred years, the thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and the distance between each two heavens is five hundred years; and in the seventh heaven is a sea whose depth is equal to all of that, in which is an angel whose ankles do not reach the water." [146] [[The beginning of the hadith is in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/314; its end is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 28/195.]]

﴿And that He is the One who makes laugh and makes weep﴾, among His creation whomever He wills.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, saying: Dallal, daughter of Abu al-Mudall, told us, saying: al-Sahba' told us, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by some people who were laughing, and he said: "If you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little." [147] Then Jibril came down to him and said: "Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And that He is the One who makes laugh and weep﴾." So he returned to them and said: "I had not taken forty steps before Jibril came and said: Go to these people and tell them: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: He makes laugh and makes weep." [148] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/116.]]

'Ata' ibn Abi Aslam said: it means: He makes joyful and makes sad, because joy brings laughter and sorrow brings weeping.

I heard Abu Mansur al-Hamsadhi say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Razi say: I heard Yusuf ibn Jubayr say: Tahir al-Maqdisi was asked: "Do the angels laugh?" He said: "Nothing has laughed beneath the Throne since Hell was created." It was said to 'Umar: "Did the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, and faith was more firmly fixed in their hearts than the firm mountains." Mujahid said: He makes the people of Paradise laugh in Paradise, and makes the people of the Fire weep in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: He makes the earth laugh with vegetation and makes the sky weep with rain. It was also said: He makes the dawns laugh with lights and makes the sky weep with showers. Dhu al-Nun said: He makes the hearts of the believers and the knowers laugh with the sun of His recognition, and makes the hearts of the disbelieving and disobedient weep with the darkness of their denial and disobedience. Sahl: He makes the obedient laugh with mercy and makes the disobedient weep with wrath. Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi: He makes the believer laugh in the Hereafter and makes him weep in this world. Qassam ibn 'Abd Allah: He makes their teeth laugh and makes their hearts weep, and he recited in its meaning:

The tongue laughs while the entrails burn,
and its laughter is only falsehood and fabrication.
O Lord, a weeper with no tears in his eye,
and a laugher whose tooth has no strength left. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/117.]]

﴿And that He is the One who causes death and gives life﴾: He causes death, meaning He annihilates in this world, and gives life for resurrection. It was said: He causes the fathers to die and gives life to the sons. It was said: He causes the drop to die and gives life to the soul. It was said: He causes the disbeliever to die through denial and severance, and gives life to the believer through recognition and connection; He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life?﴾ Al-Qasim said: He causes to die regarding His remembrance and gives life through His remembrance. Ibn 'Ata': He causes death by His justice and gives life by His grace. It was said: He causes death by withholding and stinginess, and gives life by generosity and giving.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 53, verse 33–44:

﴿Have you seen the one who turned away...﴾ ... the verses. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and al-Musayyib ibn Sharik said: it was revealed concerning 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, who used to give charity and spend in good causes. His foster brother 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Sarh said to him: "What is this that you are doing? Soon nothing will be left for you." 'Uthman said: "I have sins and wrongdoings, and by what I do I seek the pleasure of Allah and hope for His pardon." 'Abd Allah said to him: "Give me your she-camel with its saddle, and I will bear all your sins for you." So he gave it to him, and had him testify to it, and refrained from some of the charity and spending he had been doing. Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾, meaning on the day of Uhud, when he abandoned his position [[Meaning: when he abandoned the position in the battle.]].

﴿And gave a little and then withheld﴾, meaning his companion gave a little and then cut off his spending. 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, then returned to the best and finest of that (course).

Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. He had followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his religion, but some of the polytheists reproached him and said: "Have you abandoned the religion of the elders, misled them, and claimed that they are in the Fire? You should have supported them." He said: "I feared the punishment of Allah." So the one who reproached him guaranteed to him that, if he gave him some of his wealth and returned to his polytheism, he would bear the punishment of Allah for him. He did so, and gave the one who had reproached him some of what he had guaranteed, then he became miserly and withheld the rest of what he had guaranteed.

So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾, meaning turned back from faith, ﴿and gave a little﴾, meaning his companion, the guarantor, ﴿and then withheld﴾, meaning he withheld the remainder. Muqatil said: it means al-Walid gave a little good with his tongue, then ﴿withheld﴾, that is, cut it off and did not persist in it.

Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Zubaydi related from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: it was revealed concerning a man who said to his family: "Equip me, I will go to this man," meaning the Prophet ﷺ. So he equipped himself and set out, and a man from among the disbelievers met him and said: "Where are you going?" He said: "To Muhammad, perhaps I will obtain some of his goodness." The man said to him: "Give me your equipment and I will bear your sin," and this verse was revealed concerning him.

It is also related from al-Suddi that he said: it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, because he would sometimes agree with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in some matters. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, because he said: "By Allah, Muhammad only orders us to the noble qualities of character." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿gave a little and then withheld﴾, that is, he did not believe.

The exegetes said: ﴿akda﴾ means he cut it off and did not persist in it, and its origin is from al-kudya, which is a rock that appears in a well and prevents digging and makes one despair of water.

Al-Kisa'i said: the Arabs say: "akda al-hafir" and "ajbal" when the digger reaches the kudya and the mountain (rock) in digging. He also said: "kadat asabi'uhu" when they became callused, and "kadat yaduhu" when it became weary and it did nothing, and "kadā al-nabt" when its growth diminished. The historian said: ﴿akda﴾ means he withheld good. Al-Hutay'a said:

He gave a little, then withheld his gift,
and whoever gives kindness among people is praised. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/112.]]

﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees? Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Musa﴾, meaning the books of the Torah, ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾, meaning what he was sent with of conveying the message of Allah, which is His saying: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾. Ikrima and Tawus related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: before Ibrahim, peace be upon him, they used to seize a man for the sin of another, and a guardian would be seized for a guardian in killing, so that a man would be killed for his father, his brother, his son, his paternal uncle, or his maternal uncle, a husband would be killed for his wife, and a master would be killed for his slave. Then came Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he forbade them from that and conveyed to them from Allah: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾.

Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: he acted upon what he was commanded and conveyed the messages of his Lord to His creation. Mujahid said: he fulfilled what was obligated upon him. Al-Rabi': he fulfilled his vision and carried out the slaughter of his son. 'Ata' al-Khurasani: he practised obedience. Abu al-'Aliya: he fulfilled the completeness of Islam, which is His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾, and no one was tested with this religion and fulfilled all its requirements except Ibrahim. The meaning of tawfiya is completion; one says: "I fulfilled his right to him and gave it in full," and Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿that He may pay them their rewards in full﴾. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna: he discharged the trust. Al-Dahhak: he fulfilled the matter of the rites. 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib: it has reached me that Ibrahim had made a pledge not to ask anything of a created being; when he was thrown into the Fire, Jibril came to him and said: "Do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no." So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, praised him for standing by what he said and fulfilling what he had pledged, so the Mighty One said: ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: he fulfilled the matter of guests, until he was named the father of guests. Abu Bakr al-Warraq: he upheld the condition of what he claimed, because Allah, glorified is He, said to him: "Submit," and he said: "I have submitted," so Allah, glorified is He, demanded the truth of his claim, and tested him in his wealth, his children and himself, and found him fulfilling all of that. So He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾, meaning he claimed Islam, then confirmed his claim.

It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ regarding the interpretation of this verse two statements:

The first: what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: al-Qati'i told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told me, saying: Husayn told us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a told us, saying: Rayyan ibn Fa'id told us, from Sahl, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Shall I not inform you why the Exalted named Ibrahim His friend, the one who fulfilled? Because he used to say every morning and evening: ﴿Glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ until he completed the verse." [134] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 1/735.]]

The second: what

al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Maqri told us, saying: Abu 'Umar told us, saying: Nasr ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Ma'mar ibn Sulayman informed us, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, that the Prophet ﷺ recited ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾ and said:

"Do you know with what he fulfilled?" [135] They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "He fulfilled it, meaning he performed four rak'as at the beginning of his day," which he would pray from the start of the day. [136]

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, saying: Mu'awiya told us, from Abu al-Zahiriya, from Kathir ibn Murra, from Nu'aym ibn Hammar, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah the Exalted says: O son of Adam, do not fall short of four rak'as at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you for its end." [137]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Samura told us, saying: Abu Talha Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Karim told us, saying: Nasr ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mu'tasim Abu Jamil told us, from Abu Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he recited "wa-Ibrahim alladhi wafa" lightly (with a light pronunciation).

As for the reconciliation between His saying: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾ and His saying: ﴿and they will surely bear their burdens and other burdens along with their burdens﴾, it is what al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: ﴿and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾ voluntarily, and ﴿they will surely bear their burdens and other burdens along with their burdens﴾ by compulsion.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Hulwani told us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Iyad ibn Laqit told us, from Abu Ramtha, who said: I went with my father to the Prophet ﷺ. When I saw him, my father said to me: "Do you know who this is? This is the Messenger of Allah." He said: I shuddered at what he said to me, for I had thought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was something unlike people, but he was a man with abundant hair, with traces of henna on it, and he wore two green garments. My father greeted him, then we sat and talked for a while. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to my father: "Is this your son?" My father said: "By the Lord of the Ka'ba, truly, I testify to it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled, laughing at the affirmation of my resemblance to my father and at my father's oath concerning me. He said: "Indeed, he will not commit a crime against you, nor will you against him," then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾. Then my father looked at a growth like a lump between his shoulders and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a physician of men; shall I treat it for you?" He said: "No, its physician is the One who created it." [138] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 13/337; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/279.]]

﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾, meaning what he works. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: this verse is abrogated, and then Allah revealed after it: ﴿And those who believed, and whose descendants followed them in faith — We will join them with their descendants﴾, and We did not deprive them of anything, so the children enter Paradise through the righteousness of their fathers.

Ikrima said: that applied to the people of Ibrahim and Musa; as for this nation, they have what they strive for and what others strive for. [Like] the good report of Sa'd when he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Will it benefit my mother if I give charity on her behalf?" He said: "Yes" [139], and the report of the woman who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "My father died without performing Hajj." He said: "Perform Hajj on his behalf." [140]

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿And that man will have nothing﴾ means the disbeliever; as for the believer, he has what he strove for and what was striven for on his behalf. It was also said: the disbeliever has no good except what he did, for which he is rewarded in the abode of this world, so that no good remains for him in the Hereafter.

It is related that 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had given al-'Abbas a shirt, which he had dressed him in. When 'Abd Allah died, the Messenger of Allah sent his shirt so that he might be shrouded in it. Thus no good deed remained for him in the Hereafter for which he would be rewarded.

I heard Ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Mudarib say: I heard my father say: 'Abd Allah ibn Tahir, governor of Khurasan, summoned al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl and said: "Three verses have become unclear to me, so I called you to clarify them for me." He said: "What are they, O Amir?" He said: Allah's saying regarding the two sons of Adam: ﴿and he became one of the regretful﴾; and the report that is authentic: "Regret is repentance"; [141] and His saying: ﴿every day He is in a matter﴾; and the authentic report: "The pen has dried with what is to happen until the Day of Resurrection" [142]; and His saying: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾. So what is the matter with the contradictions? Al-Husayn said: It is possible that Qabil's regret was not repentance for him, while the regret of this nation is repentance for it, since Allah, glorified is He, has singled out this nation with distinctions which other nations did not share.

There is another statement: that Qabil's regret was not over killing Habil, but over carrying him. As for His saying: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾, it means by way of justice; and the sense of the verse is: "And that man will have nothing except what he strives for, justly, [and I may reward him with one thousand for one as a bounty]." As for His saying: ﴿every day He is in a matter﴾, it refers to affairs He renews, not affairs He initiates; and the sense of the verse is driving the decrees toward their appointed times. He said: Then 'Abd Allah ibn Tahir stood up, kissed his head, and granted him his revenue.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: ﴿illa ma sa'a﴾ means "intended" (nawa). Its clarification is the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "People will be resurrected according to their intentions." [143] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1414; Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/419, no. 7242.]]

﴿And that his effort will be seen; then he will be given the fullest recompense﴾. Al-Akhfash said: one says "jazaytuhu al-jaza'" and "jazaytuhu bil-jaza'", there is no difference between them. A poet said:

If I repay 'Alqama ibn Sa'd for his effort,
I would not repay him with the trial of a single day. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/115.]]

So he combined the two dialects.

He did so, and gave the one who had reproached him some of what he had guaranteed, then he became miserly and withheld the rest of what he had guaranteed.

So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾, meaning turned back from faith, ﴿and gave a little﴾, meaning his companion, the guarantor, ﴿and then withheld﴾, meaning he withheld the remainder. Muqatil said: it means al-Walid gave a little good with his tongue, then ﴿withheld﴾, that is, cut it off and did not persist in it.

Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Zubaydi related from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: it was revealed concerning a man who said to his family: "Equip me, I will go to this man," meaning the Prophet ﷺ. So he equipped himself and set out, and a man from among the disbelievers met him and said: "Where are you going?" He said: "To Muhammad, perhaps I will obtain some of his goodness." The man said to him: "Give me your equipment and I will bear your sin," and this verse was revealed concerning him.

It is also related from al-Suddi that he said: it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, because he would sometimes agree with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in some matters. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, because he said: "By Allah, Muhammad only orders us to the noble qualities of character." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿gave a little and then withheld﴾, that is, he did not believe.

The exegetes said: ﴿akda﴾ means he cut it off and did not persist in it, and its origin is from al-kudya, which is a rock that appears in a well and prevents digging and makes one despair of water.

Al-Kisa'i said: the Arabs say: "akda al-hafir" and "ajbal" when the digger reaches the kudya and the mountain (rock) in digging. He also said: "kadat asabi'uhu" when they became callused, and "kadat yaduhu" when it became weary and it did nothing, and "kadā al-nabt" when its growth diminished. The historian said: ﴿akda﴾ means he withheld good. Al-Hutay'a said:

He gave a little, then withheld his gift,
and whoever gives kindness among people is praised. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/112.]]

﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees? Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Musa﴾, meaning the books of the Torah, ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾, meaning what he was sent with of conveying the message of Allah, which is His saying: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾. Ikrima and Tawus related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: before Ibrahim, peace be upon him, they used to seize a man for the sin of another, and a guardian would be seized for a guardian in killing, so that a man would be killed for his father, his brother, his son, his paternal uncle, or his maternal uncle, a husband would be killed for his wife, and a master would be killed for his slave. Then came Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he forbade them from that and conveyed to them from Allah: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾.

Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: he acted upon what he was commanded and conveyed the messages of his Lord to His creation. Mujahid said: he fulfilled what was obligated upon him. Al-Rabi': he fulfilled his vision and carried out the slaughter of his son. 'Ata' al-Khurasani: he practised obedience. Abu al-'Aliya: he fulfilled the completeness of Islam, which is His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾, and no one was tested with this religion and fulfilled all its requirements except Ibrahim. The meaning of tawfiya is completion; one says: "I fulfilled his right to him and gave it in full," and Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿that He may pay them their rewards in full﴾. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna: he discharged the trust. Al-Dahhak: he fulfilled the matter of the rites. 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib: it has reached me that Ibrahim had made a pledge not to ask anything of a created being; when he was thrown into the Fire, Jibril came to him and said: "Do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no." So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, praised him for standing by what he said and fulfilling what he had pledged, so the Mighty One said: ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: he fulfilled the matter of guests, until he was named the father of guests. Abu Bakr al-Warraq: he upheld the condition of what he claimed, because Allah, glorified is He, said to him: "Submit," and he said: "I have submitted," so Allah, glorified is He, demanded the truth of his claim, and tested him in his wealth, his children and himself, and found him fulfilling all of that. So He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾, meaning he claimed Islam, then confirmed his claim.

It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ regarding the interpretation of this verse two statements:

The first: what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: al-Qati'i told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told me, saying: Husayn told us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a told us, saying: Rayyan ibn Fa'id told us, from Sahl, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Shall I not inform you why the Exalted named Ibrahim His friend, the one who fulfilled? Because he used to say every morning and evening: ﴿Glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ until he completed the verse." [134] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 1/735.]]

The second: what

al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Maqri told us, saying: Abu 'Umar told us, saying: Nasr ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Ma'mar ibn Sulayman informed us, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, that the Prophet ﷺ recited ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾ and said:

"Do you know with what he fulfilled?" [135] They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "He fulfilled it, meaning he performed four rak'as at the beginning of his day," which he would pray from the start of the day. [136]

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, saying: Mu'awiya told us, from Abu al-Zahiriya, from Kathir ibn Murra, from Nu'aym ibn Hammar, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah the Exalted says: O son of Adam, do not fall short of four rak'as at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you for its end." [137]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Samura told us, saying: Abu Talha Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Karim told us, saying: Nasr ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mu'tasim Abu Jamil told us, from Abu Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he recited "wa-Ibrahim alladhi wafa" lightly (with a light pronunciation).

As for the reconciliation between His saying: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾ and His saying: ﴿and they will surely bear their burdens and other burdens along with their burdens﴾, it is what al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: ﴿and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾ voluntarily, and ﴿they will surely bear their burdens and other burdens along with their burdens﴾ by compulsion.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Hulwani told us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Iyad ibn Laqit told us, from Abu Ramtha, who said: I went with my father to the Prophet ﷺ. When I saw him, my father said to me: "Do you know who this is? This is the Messenger of Allah." He said: I shuddered at what he said to me, for I had thought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was something unlike people, but he was a man with abundant hair, with traces of henna on it, and he wore two green garments. My father greeted him, then we sat and talked for a while. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to my father: "Is this your son?" My father said: "By the Lord of the Ka'ba, truly, I testify to it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled, laughing at the affirmation of my resemblance to my father and at my father's oath concerning me. He said: "Indeed, he will not commit a crime against you, nor will you against him," then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾. Then my father looked at a growth like a lump between his shoulders and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a physician of men; shall I treat it for you?" He said: "No, its physician is the One who created it." [138] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 13/337; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/279.]]

﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾, meaning what he works. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: this verse is abrogated, and then Allah revealed after it: ﴿And those who believed, and whose descendants followed them in faith — We will join them with their descendants﴾, and We did not deprive them of anything, so the children enter Paradise through the righteousness of their fathers.

Ikrima said: that applied to the people of Ibrahim and Musa; as for this nation, they have what they strive for and what others strive for. [Like] the good report of Sa'd when he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Will it benefit my mother if I give charity on her behalf?" He said: "Yes" [139], and the report of the woman who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "My father died without performing Hajj." He said: "Perform Hajj on his behalf." [140]

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿And that man will have nothing﴾ means the disbeliever; as for the believer, he has what he strove for and what was striven for on his behalf. It was also said: the disbeliever has no good except what he did, for which he is rewarded in the abode of this world, so that no good remains for him in the Hereafter.

It is related that 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had given al-'Abbas a shirt, which he had dressed him in. When 'Abd Allah died, the Messenger of Allah sent his shirt so that he might be shrouded in it. Thus no good deed remained for him in the Hereafter for which he would be rewarded.

I heard Ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Mudarib say: I heard my father say: 'Abd Allah ibn Tahir, governor of Khurasan, summoned al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl and said: "Three verses have become unclear to me, so I called you to clarify them for me." He said: "What are they, O Amir?" He said: Allah's saying regarding the two sons of Adam: ﴿and he became one of the regretful﴾; and the report that is authentic: "Regret is repentance"; [141] and His saying: ﴿every day He is in a matter﴾; and the authentic report: "The pen has dried with what is to happen until the Day of Resurrection" [142]; and His saying: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾. So what is the matter with the contradictions? Al-Husayn said: It is possible that Qabil's regret was not repentance for him, while the regret of this nation is repentance for it, since Allah, glorified is He, has singled out this nation with distinctions which other nations did not share.

There is another statement: that Qabil's regret was not over killing Habil, but over carrying him. As for His saying: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾, it means by way of justice; and the sense of the verse is: "And that man will have nothing except what he strives for, justly, [and I may reward him with one thousand for one as a bounty]." As for His saying: ﴿every day He is in a matter﴾, it refers to affairs He renews, not affairs He initiates; and the sense of the verse is driving the decrees toward their appointed times. He said: Then 'Abd Allah ibn Tahir stood up, kissed his head, and granted him his revenue.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: ﴿illa ma sa'a﴾ means "intended" (nawa). Its clarification is the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "People will be resurrected according to their intentions." [143] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1414; Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/419, no. 7242.]]

﴿And that his effort will be seen; then he will be given the fullest recompense﴾. Al-Akhfash said: one says "jazaytuhu al-jaza'" and "jazaytuhu bil-jaza'", there is no difference between them. A poet said:

If I repay 'Alqama ibn Sa'd for his effort,
I would not repay him with the trial of a single day. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/115.]]

So he combined the two dialects.

﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾, meaning the end of creation and their return; He is the one who recompenses them for their deeds. It was also said: from Him is the beginning of bounty, and to Him is the end of hopes.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sufyani informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sama' ibn Fath al-Hanbali told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Misri told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Mansur al-Sa'di told us, saying: al-'Abbas ibn Zafar told us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ, regarding His saying: ﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾, he said: "There is no reflection upon Allah." [144] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/696.]]

Evidence for this report is what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba told us, saying: 'Umayr ibn Mirdas told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Sulami told us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a told us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Sinan ibn Sa'd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is mentioned, then desist." [145] [[Musnad al-Shamiyin: 3/308, no. 2350.]]

[Akhbarana] Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Jamshadhi, by recitation, in the year 387, said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Majbur told us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya told me, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Junayd told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Mughanni told me, saying: Dawud, the paternal uncle of al-Husayn ibn Qabil, told us, from Qatada, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to his companions while they were reflecting, and he said: "What are you about?" They said: "We are reflecting upon the Creator." He said: "Reflect upon creation, and do not reflect upon the Creator, for thought cannot encompass Him. Reflect that Allah created the seven heavens and earths: the thickness of each earth is five hundred years, the distance between each two earths is five hundred years, the distance between the sky and the earth is five hundred years, the thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and the distance between each two heavens is five hundred years; and in the seventh heaven is a sea whose depth is equal to all of that, in which is an angel whose ankles do not reach the water." [146] [[The beginning of the hadith is in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/314; its end is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 28/195.]]

﴿And that He is the One who makes laugh and makes weep﴾, among His creation whomever He wills.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, saying: Dallal, daughter of Abu al-Mudall, told us, saying: al-Sahba' told us, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by some people who were laughing, and he said: "If you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little." [147] Then Jibril came down to him and said: "Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And that He is the One who makes laugh and weep﴾." So he returned to them and said: "I had not taken forty steps before Jibril came and said: Go to these people and tell them: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: He makes laugh and makes weep." [148] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/116.]]

'Ata' ibn Abi Aslam said: it means: He makes joyful and makes sad, because joy brings laughter and sorrow brings weeping.

I heard Abu Mansur al-Hamsadhi say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Razi say: I heard Yusuf ibn Jubayr say: Tahir al-Maqdisi was asked: "Do the angels laugh?" He said: "Nothing has laughed beneath the Throne since Hell was created." It was said to 'Umar: "Did the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, and faith was more firmly fixed in their hearts than the firm mountains." Mujahid said: He makes the people of Paradise laugh in Paradise, and makes the people of the Fire weep in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: He makes the earth laugh with vegetation and makes the sky weep with rain. It was also said: He makes the dawns laugh with lights and makes the sky weep with showers. Dhu al-Nun said: He makes the hearts of the believers and the knowers laugh with the sun of His recognition, and makes the hearts of the disbelieving and disobedient weep with the darkness of their denial and disobedience. Sahl: He makes the obedient laugh with mercy and makes the disobedient weep with wrath. Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi: He makes the believer laugh in the Hereafter and makes him weep in this world. Qassam ibn 'Abd Allah: He makes their teeth laugh and makes their hearts weep, and he recited in its meaning:

The tongue laughs while the entrails burn,
and its laughter is only falsehood and fabrication.
O Lord, a weeper with no tears in his eye,
and a laugher whose tooth has no strength left. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/117.]]

﴿And that He is the One who causes death and gives life﴾: He causes death, meaning He annihilates in this world, and gives life for resurrection. It was said: He causes the fathers to die and gives life to the sons. It was said: He causes the drop to die and gives life to the soul. It was said: He causes the disbeliever to die through denial and severance, and gives life to the believer through recognition and connection; He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life?﴾ Al-Qasim said: He causes to die regarding His remembrance and gives life through His remembrance. Ibn 'Ata': He causes death by His justice and gives life by His grace. It was said: He causes death by withholding and stinginess, and gives life by generosity and giving.

His foster brother 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Sarh said to him: "What is this that you are doing? Soon nothing will be left for you." 'Uthman said: "I have sins and wrongdoings, and by what I do I seek the pleasure of Allah and hope for His pardon." 'Abd Allah said to him: "Give me your she-camel with its saddle, and I will bear all your sins for you." So he gave it to him, and had him testify to it, and refrained from some of the charity and spending he had been doing. When I saw him, my father said to me: "Do you know who this is? This is the Messenger of Allah." He said: I shuddered at what he said to me, for I had thought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was something unlike people, but he was a man with abundant hair, with traces of henna on it, and he wore two green garments. My father greeted him, then we sat and talked for a while. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to my father: "Is this your son?" My father said: "By the Lord of the Ka'ba, truly, I testify to it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled, laughing at the affirmation of my resemblance to my father and at my father's oath concerning me. He said: "Indeed, he will not commit a crime against you, nor will you against him," then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾. Then my father looked at a growth like a lump between his shoulders and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a physician of men; shall I treat it for you?" He said: "No, its physician is the One who created it." [138] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 13/337; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/279.]]

﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾, meaning what he works. Its counterpart is His saying: ﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: this verse is abrogated, and then Allah revealed after it: ﴿And those who believed, and whose descendants followed them in faith — We will join them with their descendants﴾, and We did not deprive them of anything, so the children enter Paradise through the righteousness of their fathers.

Ikrima said: that applied to the people of Ibrahim and Musa; as for this nation, they have what they strive for and what others strive for. [Like] the good report of Sa'd when he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Will it benefit my mother if I give charity on her behalf?" He said: "Yes" [139], and the report of the woman who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "My father died without performing Hajj." He said: "Perform Hajj on his behalf." [140]

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: ﴿And that man will have nothing﴾ means the disbeliever; as for the believer, he has what he strove for and what was striven for on his behalf. It was also said: the disbeliever has no good except what he did, for which he is rewarded in the abode of this world, so that no good remains for him in the Hereafter.

It is related that 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy had given al-'Abbas a shirt, which he had dressed him in. When 'Abd Allah died, the Messenger of Allah sent his shirt so that he might be shrouded in it. Thus no good deed remained for him in the Hereafter for which he would be rewarded.

I heard Ibn Habib say: I heard Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Mudarib say: I heard my father say: 'Abd Allah ibn Tahir, governor of Khurasan, summoned al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl and said: "Three verses have become unclear to me, so I called you to clarify them for me." He said: "What are they, O Amir?" He said: Allah's saying regarding the two sons of Adam: ﴿and he became one of the regretful﴾; and the report that is authentic: "Regret is repentance"; [141] and His saying: ﴿every day He is in a matter﴾; and the authentic report: "The pen has dried with what is to happen until the Day of Resurrection" [142]; and His saying: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾. So what is the matter with the contradictions? Al-Husayn said: It is possible that Qabil's regret was not repentance for him, while the regret of this nation is repentance for it, since Allah, glorified is He, has singled out this nation with distinctions which other nations did not share.

There is another statement: that Qabil's regret was not over killing Habil, but over carrying him. As for His saying: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾, it means by way of justice; and the sense of the verse is: "And that man will have nothing except what he strives for, justly, [and I may reward him with one thousand for one as a bounty]." As for His saying: ﴿every day He is in a matter﴾, it refers to affairs He renews, not affairs He initiates; and the sense of the verse is driving the decrees toward their appointed times. He said: Then 'Abd Allah ibn Tahir stood up, kissed his head, and granted him his revenue.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: ﴿illa ma sa'a﴾ means "intended" (nawa). Its clarification is the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "People will be resurrected according to their intentions." [143] [[Sunan Ibn Majah: 2/1414; Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/419, no. 7242.]]

﴿And that his effort will be seen; then he will be given the fullest recompense﴾. Al-Akhfash said: one says "jazaytuhu al-jaza'" and "jazaytuhu bil-jaza'", there is no difference between them. A poet said:

If I repay 'Alqama ibn Sa'd for his effort,
I would not repay him with the trial of a single day. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/115.]]

So he combined the two dialects.

﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾, meaning the end of creation and their return; He is the one who recompenses them for their deeds. It was also said: from Him is the beginning of bounty, and to Him is the end of hopes.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sufyani informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sama' ibn Fath al-Hanbali told us, saying: 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Misri told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Mansur al-Sa'di told us, saying: al-'Abbas ibn Zafar told us, from Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ, regarding His saying: ﴿And that to your Lord is the final end﴾, he said: "There is no reflection upon Allah." [144] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/696.]]

Evidence for this report is what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shayba told us, saying: 'Umayr ibn Mirdas told us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim al-Sulami told us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a told us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Sinan ibn Sa'd, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is mentioned, then desist." [145] [[Musnad al-Shamiyin: 3/308, no. 2350.]]

[Akhbarana] Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Jamshadhi, by recitation, in the year 387, said: Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Majbur told us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Bazzaz told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya told me, saying: Ibrahim ibn al-Junayd told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Mughanni told me, saying: Dawud, the paternal uncle of al-Husayn ibn Qabil, told us, from Qatada, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to his companions while they were reflecting, and he said: "What are you about?" They said: "We are reflecting upon the Creator." He said: "Reflect upon creation, and do not reflect upon the Creator, for thought cannot encompass Him. Reflect that Allah created the seven heavens and earths: the thickness of each earth is five hundred years, the distance between each two earths is five hundred years, the distance between the sky and the earth is five hundred years, the thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and the distance between each two heavens is five hundred years; and in the seventh heaven is a sea whose depth is equal to all of that, in which is an angel whose ankles do not reach the water." [146] [[The beginning of the hadith is in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/314; its end is in Tafsir al-Tabari: 28/195.]]

﴿And that He is the One who makes laugh and makes weep﴾, among His creation whomever He wills.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told us, saying: Dallal, daughter of Abu al-Mudall, told us, saying: al-Sahba' told us, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Prophet ﷺ passed by some people who were laughing, and he said: "If you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little." [147] Then Jibril came down to him and said: "Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And that He is the One who makes laugh and weep﴾." So he returned to them and said: "I had not taken forty steps before Jibril came and said: Go to these people and tell them: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: He makes laugh and makes weep." [148] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/116.]]

'Ata' ibn Abi Aslam said: it means: He makes joyful and makes sad, because joy brings laughter and sorrow brings weeping.

I heard Abu Mansur al-Hamsadhi say: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Razi say: I heard Yusuf ibn Jubayr say: Tahir al-Maqdisi was asked: "Do the angels laugh?" He said: "Nothing has laughed beneath the Throne since Hell was created." It was said to 'Umar: "Did the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh?" He said: "Yes, by Allah, and faith was more firmly fixed in their hearts than the firm mountains." Mujahid said: He makes the people of Paradise laugh in Paradise, and makes the people of the Fire weep in the Fire. Al-Dahhak said: He makes the earth laugh with vegetation and makes the sky weep with rain. It was also said: He makes the dawns laugh with lights and makes the sky weep with showers. Dhu al-Nun said: He makes the hearts of the believers and the knowers laugh with the sun of His recognition, and makes the hearts of the disbelieving and disobedient weep with the darkness of their denial and disobedience. Sahl: He makes the obedient laugh with mercy and makes the disobedient weep with wrath. Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Tirmidhi: He makes the believer laugh in the Hereafter and makes him weep in this world. Qassam ibn 'Abd Allah: He makes their teeth laugh and makes their hearts weep, and he recited in its meaning:

The tongue laughs while the entrails burn,
and its laughter is only falsehood and fabrication.
O Lord, a weeper with no tears in his eye,
and a laugher whose tooth has no strength left. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/117.]]

﴿And that He is the One who causes death and gives life﴾: He causes death, meaning He annihilates in this world, and gives life for resurrection. It was said: He causes the fathers to die and gives life to the sons. It was said: He causes the drop to die and gives life to the soul. It was said: He causes the disbeliever to die through denial and severance, and gives life to the believer through recognition and connection; He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life?﴾ Al-Qasim said: He causes to die regarding His remembrance and gives life through His remembrance. Ibn 'Ata': He causes death by His justice and gives life by His grace. It was said: He causes death by withholding and stinginess, and gives life by generosity and giving.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 53, verse 33–44:

﴿Have you seen the one who turned away...﴾ ... the verses. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and al-Musayyib ibn Sharik said: it was revealed concerning 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, who used to give charity and spend in good causes. His foster brother 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Sarh said to him: "What is this that you are doing? Soon nothing will be left for you." 'Uthman said: "I have sins and wrongdoings, and by what I do I seek the pleasure of Allah and hope for His pardon." 'Abd Allah said to him: "Give me your she-camel with its saddle, and I will bear all your sins for you." So he gave it to him, and had him testify to it, and refrained from some of the charity and spending he had been doing. Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾, meaning on the day of Uhud, when he abandoned his position [[Meaning: when he abandoned the position in the battle.]].

﴿And gave a little and then withheld﴾, meaning his companion gave a little and then cut off his spending. 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, then returned to the best and finest of that (course).

Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. He had followed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his religion, but some of the polytheists reproached him and said: "Have you abandoned the religion of the elders, misled them, and claimed that they are in the Fire? You should have supported them." He said: "I feared the punishment of Allah." So the one who reproached him guaranteed to him that, if he gave him some of his wealth and returned to his polytheism, he would bear the punishment of Allah for him. He did so, and gave the one who had reproached him some of what he had guaranteed, then he became miserly and withheld the rest of what he had guaranteed.

So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Have you seen the one who turned away﴾, meaning turned back from faith, ﴿and gave a little﴾, meaning his companion, the guarantor, ﴿and then withheld﴾, meaning he withheld the remainder. Muqatil said: it means al-Walid gave a little good with his tongue, then ﴿withheld﴾, that is, cut it off and did not persist in it.

Musa ibn 'Ubayda al-Zubaydi related from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: it was revealed concerning a man who said to his family: "Equip me, I will go to this man," meaning the Prophet ﷺ. So he equipped himself and set out, and a man from among the disbelievers met him and said: "Where are you going?" He said: "To Muhammad, perhaps I will obtain some of his goodness." The man said to him: "Give me your equipment and I will bear your sin," and this verse was revealed concerning him.

It is also related from al-Suddi that he said: it was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, because he would sometimes agree with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in some matters. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, because he said: "By Allah, Muhammad only orders us to the noble qualities of character." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿gave a little and then withheld﴾, that is, he did not believe.

The exegetes said: ﴿akda﴾ means he cut it off and did not persist in it, and its origin is from al-kudya, which is a rock that appears in a well and prevents digging and makes one despair of water.

Al-Kisa'i said: the Arabs say: "akda al-hafir" and "ajbal" when the digger reaches the kudya and the mountain (rock) in digging. He also said: "kadat asabi'uhu" when they became callused, and "kadat yaduhu" when it became weary and it did nothing, and "kadā al-nabt" when its growth diminished. The historian said: ﴿akda﴾ means he withheld good. Al-Hutay'a said:

He gave a little, then withheld his gift,
and whoever gives kindness among people is praised. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 17/112.]]

﴿Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so that he sees? Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Musa﴾, meaning the books of the Torah, ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾, meaning what he was sent with of conveying the message of Allah, which is His saying: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾. Ikrima and Tawus related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: before Ibrahim, peace be upon him, they used to seize a man for the sin of another, and a guardian would be seized for a guardian in killing, so that a man would be killed for his father, his brother, his son, his paternal uncle, or his maternal uncle, a husband would be killed for his wife, and a master would be killed for his slave. Then came Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and he forbade them from that and conveyed to them from Allah: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾.

Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: he acted upon what he was commanded and conveyed the messages of his Lord to His creation. Mujahid said: he fulfilled what was obligated upon him. Al-Rabi': he fulfilled his vision and carried out the slaughter of his son. 'Ata' al-Khurasani: he practised obedience. Abu al-'Aliya: he fulfilled the completeness of Islam, which is His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with words, and he fulfilled them﴾, and no one was tested with this religion and fulfilled all its requirements except Ibrahim. The meaning of tawfiya is completion; one says: "I fulfilled his right to him and gave it in full," and Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿that He may pay them their rewards in full﴾. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna: he discharged the trust. Al-Dahhak: he fulfilled the matter of the rites. 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib: it has reached me that Ibrahim had made a pledge not to ask anything of a created being; when he was thrown into the Fire, Jibril came to him and said: "Do you have any need?" He said: "As for you, no." So Allah, glorified and exalted is He, praised him for standing by what he said and fulfilling what he had pledged, so the Mighty One said: ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: he fulfilled the matter of guests, until he was named the father of guests. Abu Bakr al-Warraq: he upheld the condition of what he claimed, because Allah, glorified is He, said to him: "Submit," and he said: "I have submitted," so Allah, glorified is He, demanded the truth of his claim, and tested him in his wealth, his children and himself, and found him fulfilling all of that. So He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾, meaning he claimed Islam, then confirmed his claim.

It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ regarding the interpretation of this verse two statements:

The first: what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: al-Qati'i told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told me, saying: Husayn told us, saying: Ibn Lahi'a told us, saying: Rayyan ibn Fa'id told us, from Sahl, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Shall I not inform you why the Exalted named Ibrahim His friend, the one who fulfilled? Because he used to say every morning and evening: ﴿Glory be to Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning﴾ until he completed the verse." [134] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 1/735.]]

The second: what

al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Maqri told us, saying: Abu 'Umar told us, saying: Nasr ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Ma'mar ibn Sulayman informed us, from Ja'far, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umama, that the Prophet ﷺ recited ﴿and Ibrahim who fulfilled﴾ and said:

"Do you know with what he fulfilled?" [135] They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "He fulfilled it, meaning he performed four rak'as at the beginning of his day," which he would pray from the start of the day. [136]

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ibn Malik told us, saying: Ibn Hanbal told us, saying: my father told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, saying: Mu'awiya told us, from Abu al-Zahiriya, from Kathir ibn Murra, from Nu'aym ibn Hammar, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah the Exalted says: O son of Adam, do not fall short of four rak'as at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you for its end." [137]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Samura told us, saying: Abu Talha Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Karim told us, saying: Nasr ibn 'Ali told us, saying: al-Mu'ammar ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Mu'tasim Abu Jamil told us, from Abu Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he recited "wa-Ibrahim alladhi wafa" lightly (with a light pronunciation).

As for the reconciliation between His saying: ﴿that no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾ and His saying: ﴿and they will surely bear their burdens and other burdens along with their burdens﴾, it is what al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: ﴿and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾ voluntarily, and ﴿they will surely bear their burdens and other burdens along with their burdens﴾ by compulsion.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Hulwani told us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid told us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Iyad ibn Laqit told us, from Abu Ramtha, who said: I went with my father to the Prophet ﷺ. When I saw him, my father said to me: "Do you know who this is? This is the Messenger of Allah." He said: I shuddered at what he said to me, for I had thought the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was something unlike people, but he was a man with abundant hair, with traces of henna on it, and he wore two green garments. My father greeted him, then we sat and talked for a while. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to my father: "Is this your son?" My father said: "By the Lord of the Ka'ba, truly, I testify to it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled, laughing at the affirmation of my resemblance to my father and at my father's oath concerning me. He said: "Indeed, he will not commit a crime against you, nor will you against him," then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿and no bearer of burden shall bear the burden of another﴾. Then my father looked at a growth like a lump between his shoulders and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am a physician of men; shall I treat it for you?" He said: "No, its physician is the One who created it." [138] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 13/337; al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 22/279.]]
